etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French mode (masculine), from Latin modus (“measure, due measure, rhythm, melody”). Doublet of modus.

definitions.definition: (music) One of several ancient Greek scales.
(music) One of several common scales in modern Western music, one of which corresponds to the modern major scale and one to the natural minor scale.
A particular means of accomplishing something.

quote.citation: 1855, Journal of the Royal Horticultural Society, volume 9, page 205:
quote.text: An effectual and inexpensive mode of Protecting Wall-Trees from Spring-Frosts.

definitions.definition: A particular state of being, or frame of mind.
(statistics) The most frequently occurring value in a distribution.
(especially engineering) A state related to signals or vibrations
(mathematics, physics) A state of a system that is represented by an eigenfunction of that system.
(computing) One of various related sets of rules for processing data; more generally, any state of the system associated with certain behaviours.
(electronics) A series of settings on a device used for a specific purpose.

quote.citation: 2024 May 4, Mat Gallagher, “I tried Mercedes’ new autonomous driving in busy city streets – it's mind-blowing”, in T3‎[1]:
quote.text: The car was then placed into its Level 2 driving mode, much like you would for the current adaptive cruise control systems.

definitions.definition: (video games) A variation in gameplay, such as a difficulty level.

quote.citation: 2017 October 17, Jonathan M. Gitlin, “Gran Turismo Sport is extremely limited in offline mode”, in Ars Technica‎[2]:
quote.text: Campaign mode (the career mode that includes the notorious Gran Turismo driving school) is off limits while offline. Also unavailable offline: buying new cars, viewing your garage, editing car liveries, and even the "taking photos of fancy cars in exotic scenery" mode.

quote.citation: 2018 March 6, Martin Robinson, “Dispelling the myths of Bloodborne”, in Eurogamer‎[3]:
quote.text: I've stumbled over gaming's simplest hurdles, been humiliated by the lowliest of enemies and will often go for an easy mode if one's available, and yet I've run through Bloodborne twice without ever really breaking much of a sweat.

quote.citation: 2019 February 25, Jordan Erica Webber, “Point and shoot: what's next for photography in video games?”, in The Guardian‎[4]:
quote.text: Selfie modes, meanwhile, let you add filters and change characters’ facial expressions, from Link in The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker to Arthur Morgan in Red Dead Redemption 2.

definitions.definition: (grammar) A verb form that depends on how its containing clause relates to the speaker’s or writer’s wish, intent, or assertion about reality.
(philosophy) That which exists only as a quality of substance.
(textiles) In lace-making, a small decorative piece inserted into a pattern.
(textiles) The openwork between the solid parts of a pattern.
(obsolete) A woman's mantle with a hood.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French mode f (“fashion, trend”).

quote.citation: 1922, Edith Van Dyne, chapter 4, in Mary Louise and Josie O'Gorman:
quote.text: The dress she wore was no longer a cheap blue serge but a handsome tricolette, richly trimmed according to the prevailing mode.
